panels.title: Transaction Apply Failed Rate [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Transactions that fail during the apply (transactor) stage, per second — i.e. the transactor ran but the result was not tesSUCCESS.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of tx.transactor spans at the apply stage whose ter_result is not tesSUCCESS, over the dashboard rate interval, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*A steady low background is normal (tefPAST_SEQ, tecUNFUNDED, etc.); the transactor legitimately rejects many transactions.*

###### Healthy range:
*A low, stable rate; workload-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*A sharp rise above baseline, which points to a submission pattern that is systematically failing at apply.*

###### Keywords:
- **Transactor** *(per node)* — the rippled component that executes one transaction's type-specific logic against the ledger.
- **Transaction result codes** *(network-wide)* — the outcome code a transaction returns — tesSUCCESS, or a tec/tef/tem/ter/tel class code on failure.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as a trace span, turned into a metric by the collector (SpanMetrics connector), then aggregated by the Grafana query.*

###### Source:
[Transactor.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/tx/detail/Transactor.cpp)

###### Function:
`Transactor::operator()`

###### References:
[Transactor](https://xrpl.org/docs/references/protocol/transactions/transaction-results) · [Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#transactor)

panels.title: Transaction Processing Latency by Type
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The 95th-percentile time to process a transaction, broken down by transaction type.*

###### How it's computed:
*95th-percentile of processing durations over 5 minutes, grouped by transaction type and node.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; compare types to find the expensive ones.*

###### Healthy range:
*A few milliseconds for simple payments; workload- and type-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*A type whose latency climbs, pointing to expensive processing or resource pressure.*

###### Keywords:
- **Transaction type** *(network-wide)* — the kind of transaction (Payment, OfferCreate, TrustSet, AMM*, NFToken*, etc.), used as a breakdown dimension.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as a trace span, turned into a metric by the collector (SpanMetrics connector), then aggregated by the Grafana query.*

panels.title: Transaction Receive vs Suppressed
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Raw transactions received from peers, split by whether they were duplicates suppressed before processing.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of received transactions over the window, split by suppressed flag and node.*

###### Reading it:
*A large suppressed share is normal, since the same transaction arrives from many peers.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; suppressed typically exceeds newly processed.*

###### Watch for:
*A collapse in suppression (duplicate filtering failing) or an overall receive flood.*

###### Keywords:
- **Transaction suppression** *(per node)* — dropping a transaction already seen from another peer, so it is not reprocessed.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as a trace span, turned into a metric by the collector (SpanMetrics connector), then aggregated by the Grafana query.*

[PeerImp.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp)

###### Function:
`PeerImp::handleTransaction`

panels.title: TxQ Accept: Applied Ratio per Node (State Timeline)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The applied fraction of TxQ accepts per node over time: the share of queued transactions that were included in a ledger versus removed on failure.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per node, applied accepts divided by applied-plus-failed accepts over the window.*

###### Reading it:
*Green (>=90% applied) is a healthy drain; yellow is degraded; red means accepts are mostly failing.*

###### Healthy range:
*At or near 100% applied when the queue is draining healthily; workload-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*A node dropping into yellow or red, which signals queue pressure, under-bidding, or fee escalation on that node.*

###### Keywords:
- **Transaction queue (TxQ)** *(per node)* — holds transactions that meet local cost but not the open-ledger cost, to include in a later ledger.
- **Queue accept (drain)** *(per node)* — moving queued transactions into a newly closed ledger; the applied share shows drain health.
- **Fee escalation** *(per node)* — the exponential rise in the open-ledger cost once the ledger exceeds its soft transaction target.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as a trace span, turned into a metric by the collector (SpanMetrics connector), then aggregated by the Grafana query.*

###### Source:
[TxQ.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/detail/TxQ.cpp)

###### Function:
`TxQ::accept`

###### References:
[Transaction queue (TxQ)](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/transactions/transaction-queue) · [Fee escalation](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/transactions/transaction-cost#open-ledger-cost) · [Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#transaction-queue-txq)

**How it's computed:** Per-second rate per stage over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** A decline from earlier to later stages shows where transactions are filtered.

**Watch for:** A large early-stage drop means many transactions fail basic checks, consistent with malformed floods.

panels.title: TxQ Enqueue Rate by Transaction Type
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How many transactions are queued (rather than applied immediately) per second, by type.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of queue-enqueue operations over 5 minutes, grouped by transaction type and node.*

###### Reading it:
*Shows the demand mix hitting the queue and how it shifts as the queue fills.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; low or zero when the network is not congested.*

###### Watch for:
*A spam burst of one type, an early indicator of fee escalation.*

###### Keywords:
- **Direct apply vs enqueue** *(per node)* — whether a transaction applied straight to the open ledger or was placed in the queue for a later ledger.
- **Transaction type** *(network-wide)* — the kind of transaction (Payment, OfferCreate, TrustSet, AMM*, NFToken*, etc.), used as a breakdown dimension.
- **Fee escalation** *(per node)* — the exponential rise in the open-ledger cost once the ledger exceeds its soft transaction target.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as a trace span, turned into a metric by the collector (SpanMetrics connector), then aggregated by the Grafana query.*

[TxQ.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/detail/TxQ.cpp)

panels.title: Queue Cleanup Rate (Expired Entries)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How often expired transactions are removed from the queue each ledger, per second.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of queue-cleanup operations over 5 minutes, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Low is healthy; a rising rate means submitters are abandoning transactions.*

###### Healthy range:
*Near zero when not congested; workload-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*A rising rate, a demand-frustration signal where submitters under-bid the escalating fee and gave up.*

###### Keywords:
- **Queue expiry / abandonment** *(per node)* — removing a queued transaction whose LastLedgerSequence deadline passed before inclusion.
- **Fee escalation** *(per node)* — the exponential rise in the open-ledger cost once the ledger exceeds its soft transaction target.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as a trace span, turned into a metric by the collector (SpanMetrics connector), then aggregated by the Grafana query.*
